title: Fucoidan oligosaccharides alleviated alcoholic liver fibrosis by blocking the core fucosylation of TGF-beta receptors via the JAK/STAT3/FUT8 axis.
authors: Wang, Guifa; Zhou, Yifan; Liu, Yuhan; Zhang, Nan; Qiu, Xia; Zhou, Zijian; Pu, Yexin; Liang, Hui; Xue, Meilan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究褐藻寡糖通过JAK/STAT3/FUT8轴阻断TGF-β受体核心岩藻糖化缓解酒精性肝纤维化，核心为肝病机制与信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Alcoholic liver fibrosis (ALF) is a severe hepatic disorder caused by chronic excessive alcohol consumption, involving hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation. Fucoidan oligosaccharides (FOS) are marine algae-derived oligosaccharides with diverse biological activities. This study investigated FOS's protective effects against ALF and its molecular mechanisms through in vivo and in vitro experiments. The results indicated that FOS ameliorated liver function injury in mice. FOS reduced serum levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) while increasing the levels of alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH). FOS alleviated hepatic steatosis and inflammation, and reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and blood lipid levels. Moreover, FOS inhibited the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), downregulated the expression of alpha-smooth muscle actin (alpha-SMA), Collagen - I, and Collagen - III. Bioinformatic analysis integrating five databases with Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses revealed that Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription-3 (STAT3) is the upstream regulatory gene of fucosyltransferase 8 (FUT8) and closely associates with the Janus Kinase (JAK)/STAT signaling pathway. Molecular docking results indicated that FOS could bind to JAK1 (binding energy = -5.4 kcal/mol). Further experimental studies demonstrated that FOS downregulated the expression of FUT8 and the core fucosylation of TGF-beta type I receptor (ALK5) by inhibiting the JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway, thereby suppressing the activity of the TGF-beta/Smad signaling pathway. These results demonstrate that FOS, as a natural marine algae-derived functional oligosaccharide, exhibits potential to ameliorate ALF through suppression of the JAK/STAT3/FUT8 axis.
abstract_zh: 酒精性肝纤维化（ALF）是一种由长期过量饮酒引起的严重肝脏疾病，涉及肝星状细胞（HSCs）的激活。岩藻寡糖（FOS）是源自海洋藻类的寡糖，具有多种生物活性。本研究通过体内和体外实验探讨了FOS对ALF的保护作用及其分子机制。结果表明，FOS改善了小鼠的肝功能损伤。FOS降低了血清中丙氨酸氨基转移酶（ALT）和天冬氨酸氨基转移酶（AST）的水平，同时提高了乙醇脱氢酶（ADH）和乙醛脱氢酶（ALDH）的水平。FOS减轻了肝脏脂肪变性和炎症，并减少了肝脏脂质积累和血脂水平。此外，FOS抑制了肝星状细胞（HSCs）的激活，下调了α-平滑肌肌动蛋白（alpha-SMA）、I型胶原（Collagen-I）和III型胶原（Collagen-III）的表达。结合五个数据库与基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）通路分析的生物信息学分析揭示，信号转导与转录激活因子3（STAT3）是岩藻糖基转移酶8（FUT8）的上游调控基因，并与Janus激酶（JAK）/STAT信号通路密切相关。分子对接结果表明，FOS能与JAK1结合（结合能 = -5.4 kcal/mol）。进一步的实验研究表明，FOS通过抑制JAK/STAT3信号通路下调FUT8的表达及TGF-β I型受体（ALK5）的核心岩藻糖基化，从而抑制TGF-β/Smad信号通路的活性。这些结果表明，FOS作为一种天然的海洋藻类来源的功能性寡糖，通过抑制JAK/STAT3/FUT8轴展现出改善ALF的潜力。
